skill.name: ddd-context-mapping
skill.description: Map bounded context relationships, integration ownership, translation rules, and coupling risks using DDD context mapping patterns.
skill.summary: Create DDD context maps that clarify bounded context relationships, contract ownership, and anti-corruption boundaries.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to see ownership, dependencies, and translation needs between bounded contexts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to produce context maps, contract ownership, ACL decisions, and coupling risks.
actual_capabilities: Lists context pairs with upstream and downstream dependency direction.
Selects DDD relationship patterns such as Partnership, Shared Kernel, and Customer-Supplier.
Defines translation rules and anti-corruption layer boundaries.
Creates a contract ownership matrix for integrated contexts.
Identifies coupling risks, failure modes, fallbacks, and versioning policy.
limitations: Does not replace detailed API schema design or formal contract tests.
Requires accurate context names, ownership, and dependency information from the user.
Does not resolve team alignment or governance decisions by itself.
Best for multi-context systems, not single-context applications.

use_cases.title: Plan Service Boundaries
use_cases.description: Map how services depend on each other before teams commit to ownership and contract boundaries.

use_cases.title: Design Migration ACLs
use_cases.description: Plan anti-corruption layers when a new bounded context must consume legacy models or events.

use_cases.title: Clarify Contract Ownership
use_cases.description: Assign upstream and downstream responsibility for shared APIs, events, and published languages.

prompt_templates.title: Map New Contexts
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner mapping for a small set of contexts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these bounded contexts: Checkout, Billing, Inventory, and Fraud. Show dependency direction, relationship pattern, contract owner, and translation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Find ACL Needs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of integrations that may leak domain language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this integration list and identify where an anti-corruption layer is needed: [paste contexts and APIs]. Include coupling risks and mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Migration Contracts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a monolith-to-services migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a context map for a migration from a monolith to services. Include upstream ownership, downstream ownership, fallbacks, and versioning policy.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced critique of a proposed context map.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this architecture proposal as a DDD reviewer. Challenge each context relationship, identify weak ownership assumptions, and recommend safer contract patterns.

output_examples.input: Map Checkout, Billing, Inventory, and Fraud contexts.
output: A relationship map shows Billing as upstream for payment contracts and Inventory as upstream for stock availability.
Checkout owns local customer intent and translates Billing and Inventory terms at its boundary.
Fraud is modeled as Customer-Supplier with explicit decision contract ownership.

output_examples.input: Plan an anti-corruption layer for legacy Billing feeding new Checkout.
output: The legacy Billing model should not enter Checkout domain services directly.
An ACL translates invoice, payment status, and credit terms into Checkout language.
Contract tests should protect mapped behavior during migration.

output_examples.input: Review a context map for coupling risks.
output: The map highlights shared database access as a high coupling risk.
It recommends a Published Language for stable events and clear ownership for breaking changes.
Fallback behavior is documented for unavailable upstream contexts.

best_practices: Provide context names, owners, dependency direction, and current integration mechanisms.
Separate domain translation choices from transport or infrastructure decisions.
Revisit maps when team ownership, contracts, or release cadence changes.
anti_patterns: Using context mapping to choose cloud services or deployment tools.
Skipping contract ownership because the integration already exists.
Treating a Shared Kernel as the default pattern for unrelated teams.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces relationship maps, contract ownership decisions, translation boundaries, and coupling risk notes for bounded contexts.

faq.question: Can it design API schemas?
faq.answer: No. It can clarify ownership and translation needs, but detailed API schema design remains separate work.

faq.question: Does it support anti-corruption layers?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps identify where ACLs are needed and what language should be translated at boundaries.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide bounded context names, owners, dependency direction, current integrations, and known pain points.

faq.question: Can it evaluate an existing architecture?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review an existing context map and identify weak ownership, leakage, and coupling risks.

faq.question: Is this only for microservices?
faq.answer: No. It works for any system with multiple bounded contexts and meaningful integration boundaries.
